findings.claim: Small irregular fixation movements are called fixational drift.
findings.problem: This definition also describes rapid microsaccades and does not give the smooth continuous motion that identifies drift. A novice can infer that all small fixation movements fall under this term.
findings.repair: Say: Between brief, rapid eye movements, the eyes make small, smooth, irregular movements called fixational drift. Keep the existing term markup and retinal explanation.

metadata_judgment: Chapter title, purpose, section IDs/order and summaries match the inspected frontmatter. First-teaching records point to line21 for drift and line29 for place cell/place field. paragraph_judgments.reason: Plausible observable tasks, followed by a research question rather than a claim of experimental proof. Consistent with 2012 introduction p.1 and 2025 introduction pp.1110-1111.

Computational and systems neuroscience is accurately introduced through representation, models, recordings and behavior. Does not claim each paper collects recordings. See 2025 introduction p.1110 and the three study designs.
The three limitations correspond to the problems actually investigated. Modal wording may is appropriate. Sources: 2012 p.1, 2022 p.2, 2025 pp.1110-1111.
Continuous quantities and persistent activity are the specific subject; its status as a proposed mechanism is retained. 2012 p.1 introduction.

Continuous family, stochastic signals, weak fluctuations, analytic result, simulation check, and relation to an ideal observer match 2012 pp.1-3 and Fig.2. Plain random-times wording does not assert every form of neural variability is covered.

Lower-bound direction matches Eq.4 p.3; diminishing readout returns match Eq.5 and Fig.3 p.4. Error growth is appropriately qualitative, not an assertion of linear growth forever. Boundaries and state dependence matter at long delays, as the connected chapters teach. Keep model conditions and no anchoring input qualification; avoid later strengthening this to an unrestricted or indefinitely linear claim.

Retinal-image motivation is sound. Definition is too broad to distinguish drift from other small irregular fixation movements; original paper p.2 defines continuous smooth motion between microsaccades.

57 OMNs, two macaques, paired neural/eye measurements, calibration on larger movement, application during fixation and a separate circuit model are supported by 2022 Results p.2, Fig.2 p.4 and model pp.6-8. One-cell comparison preserves recording design.

paragraph_judgments.kind: Eye inferred result, interpretation, and limit
paragraph_judgments.reason: 0.82 weighted estimate concerns horizontal displacement variance over 350 ms, not path length or direct integrator recordings. Calibration and covariance assumptions are retained; upstream inference is distinguished from specific circuit origin. 2022 Fig.2F p.4, p.5 common-source text, Methods Eqs.11-16 p.10, Discussion p.9. Omission of the weighted error is acceptable for an about estimate in orientation.

Spatially elevated activity, connected fields, classical small-environment view and larger-environment heterogeneity match 2025 introduction pp.1110-1111. Definitions are consistent with Chapter1; later rate-map construction remains necessary.

Thresholded spatial random-function model, derivation, simulations and reused datasets are supported. Final sentence generalizes the 1D size-and-gap fitting scheme to the whole multidimensional comparison, whose parameter summaries differ.

paragraph_judgments.kind: Place model result and wiring interpretation
paragraph_judgments.reason: Size distributions, multiple peaks and holes are model predictions tested through figures 1-3 and related shape/topology comparisons, not unique connectivity measurements. Wiring remains a possible origin, matching pp.1117-1118 Discussion. Model assumptions and exact/limiting distinction remain for Chapter5.

Accurately separates theorem, inference and statistical model; no claim that these studies jointly test one circuit. Chapter6 explicitly presents the joint construction as a guide calculation and further research.
